description: City will engage community garden collective on future relocation.
This seeks preferred communication methods for future moves.
The current garden site is temporary until 2026.

chips.text: Approved
5 for, 0 against
Delegate criticized city's slow, inflexible community consultation process.
Rotary Community Garden Collective and unhoused people are affected.
Delegate noted disparity in city support for garden versus unhoused people.
Garden grows in bins due to likely contaminated soil at both locations.
Administration committed to developing an engagement plan with garden collective.

segments.title: Community Garden Relocation Presentation
segments.takeaway: A speaker presented on the community garden relocation, highlighting challenges faced by gardeners and unhoused people, and advocating for improved community consultation processes.

segments.title: Councillor Timon's Questions on Consultation and Future Sites
segments.takeaway: Councillor Timon questioned the speaker about lessons learned from the relocation process and potential future sites for the community garden, emphasizing the need for better consultation.

segments.title: Mayor Block's Questions on Garden's Future and Contamination
segments.takeaway: The Mayor inquired about the garden's preference to remain in its current temporary location and the challenges of gardening on potentially contaminated soil, seeking long-term solutions.

segments.title: Administration's Response on Stakeholder Engagement
segments.takeaway: Administration clarified that the garden collective is a noted stakeholder and an engagement plan will be developed, but cautioned on early engagement without clear direction on land use.

segments.title: Administration on Temporary Community Garden Site Process
segments.takeaway: Administration explained the process for managing community gardens on temporary sites, including working with landowners and departments to identify future plans and alternative locations.

segments.title: Motion for Preferred Communication Approaches
segments.takeaway: A motion was introduced to direct administration to engage with the garden collective to determine preferred communication and engagement approaches before developing a formal relocation process.

segments.title: Vote on Engagement Motion
segments.takeaway: The motion directing administration to engage with the garden collective on preferred communication methods for relocation was passed unanimously by the council.

segments.title: Public Speaker - Riversdale BID
segments.takeaway: Randy Shabailo from Riversdale BID requested inclusion of Riversdale in safety planning and a new street activity baseline study, highlighting the area's specific challenges.

segments.title: Questions for Public Speaker

segments.title: Questions for Administration
segments.takeaway: Committee members asked administration about the long-term nature of the safety projects, budget integration, and the potential for similar reviews for other areas like Riversdale.

segments.title: Motion to Forward Report to Budget
segments.takeaway: Councillor Parker moved to forward the safety considerations report to budget deliberations as part of the business plan option for plan implementation, which passed unanimously.

description: Requires report on program guidelines and thresholds.

chips.text: Approved
5 for, 0 against
Councillor Parker questioned the report's completeness and lack of city-wide turf assessment.
Residents near Perially Park, especially those with homes backing onto it.
Council extended the pilot and requested more reporting than administration initially proposed.
Reintroduction of targeted herbicide use after a city-wide ban since 2004.
Full long-term effectiveness of the pilot project remains to be assessed next year.
Public speakers strongly opposed herbicide use
Speakers cited federal court rulings and lawsuits regarding glyphosate and other herbicides.
Herbicide application in the pilot reportedly killed harmless pollinator plants.

segments.title: Administration presents turf remediation program
segments.takeaway: Administration proposes an ongoing turf remediation program using horticultural practices and targeted herbicide use, with financial implications for the upcoming budget.

segments.title: Public comments: Mallory Maloof opposes herbicide use
segments.takeaway: A resident opposes the pilot project and city plans to resume herbicide spraying, citing health risks, lack of transparency, and the pilot's failure.

segments.title: Public comments: Victoria Obedkov urges moratorium on herbicide use
segments.takeaway: A resident urges a moratorium on herbicide use, citing health risks, legal precedents, and the city's commitment to reducing pesticide use.

segments.title: Committee questions administration on pilot costs and scope
segments.takeaway: Committee members question administration about the pilot project's costs, the scope of future herbicide use, and the differences in turf conditions in new versus established parks.

segments.title: Committee questions administration on turf assessment and safety guidelines
segments.takeaway: Committee questions administration on the lack of a comprehensive turf assessment program, the effectiveness of the pilot, and the safety guidelines followed during herbicide application.

segments.title: Committee questions administration on herbicide necessity for severe weed issues
segments.takeaway: Committee asks if herbicide is necessary for parks with severe weed infestations and clarifies the classification of nuisance versus noxious weeds.

segments.title: Motion to extend pilot and develop comprehensive guidelines
segments.takeaway: A motion is made to extend the pilot project, integrate public feedback, respond to challenges, and develop a complete report on future program guidelines and thresholds.

segments.title: Friendly amendment to motion on guidelines and resident feedback
segments.takeaway: The motion is amended to include attaching guidelines to the budget request and surveying residents adjacent to application areas before and after remediation.
